name: Ripley
text: The bazaar opened with ten stalls and no departures; the graveyard remains empty. Gandalf’s question to Sherlock about troubling silence asks for taste, while Morpheus asks for standards—both are valid. I ask Sherlock: do you consider any merchant’s absence from today’s first words a sign of caution or strategy?

name: Ripley
text: I ask Yoda which merchant on the roster still stands silent after Sherlock’s question this morning.

name: Ripley
text: I ask Batman: your forecast that the Detective will act tonight contradicts the Compact’s plain wording. The Herald’s morning edition confirms power roles act only after today’s vote; the roster shows no night duties yet. State the clause or fact that bends that rule—because silence about the Family is not evidence, and the bazaar keeps its ledger in daylight.

name: Ripley
text: I ask Batman: six merchants pressed you for the clause or public fact that bends the Compact’s plain wording, yet you cite none. The bazaar’s Compact is short; the Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote. Produce the clause or drop the claim. Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Elsa and Sherlock asked you the same—silence has not answered.

name: Ripley
text: If Morpheus is honest, his vote tonight will cite Sherlock’s roster question and not chase a silent merchant—watch whether it does.

name: Ripley
text: If Sherlock is honest, Sherlock’s vote tonight will list every merchant named in the roster and not invent a silent one—watch whether it does.

name: Ripley
text: If Batman is honest, his vote tonight will name the Compact clause he claims exists or openly retract the forecast that the Detective acts before the vote — he has dodged nine plain demands already. Gandalf, your citation of Compact clause 5 settles the rule: the Doctor's and Detective's duties follow the vote, not precede it; the roster and the Herald both confirm ten voices today. Sherlock's conditional vote test stands firm: if you're honest, your vote will list every merchant named in the roster and not invent a silent one. The bazaar keeps its words exact — no missteps, no silence to hide behind.
